blogTitle: Design Principles in Art: Simple Rules for Better Wall Displays
videoTitle: Design Principles in Art: Simple Rules for Better Wall Displays
script:
Design Principles in Art: Simple Rules for Better Wall Displays

[warmly] You know that feeling when you step back from your wall and something just… doesn't quite sit right? That's exactly what design principles can fix.

Okay — so the first thing to understand is BALANCE… and it's not just about making both sides look the same.

A large bold piece on one side can be balanced by a CLUSTER of smaller, softer pieces on the other — it's all about visual weight, not just size.

And then there's SCALE — this one trips people up all the time, honestly.

Too small and your art just… disappears. Too large and it overwhelms everything around it. Scale makes a display feel INTENTIONAL.

Here's the thing — when you apply these visual principles, your wall stops being 'just decoration' and starts COMMUNICATING something.

You get harmony, a proper focal point, a natural flow for the eye… and your PERSONALITY comes through without it feeling chaotic.

Now — contrast and harmony… this is honestly one of the trickiest parts, but also one of my FAVOURITES.

Contrast without chaos means letting ONE piece stand out — a darker frame, a bolder print — while everything else stays calm around it.

And harmony within contrast just means your pieces AGREE on something — a colour, a mood, a style — even if they're very different from each other.

[excited] Okay, gallery walls — a little tip I love: START with a layout on the floor before you put a single nail in the wall.

Plan your layout — arrange the frames on the floor first, step back, swap things around… trust me, it saves SO much patching later.

Then choose a CONSISTENT colour story — it doesn't mean all matching, just that every piece shares at least one common tone.

Now — these principles work DIFFERENTLY depending on the style of your wall… so let's look at a couple of examples.

Classic and traditional walls tend to love SYMMETRY — think matching frames, a central hero piece, warm rich tones, and a sense of order.

Contemporary minimalist spaces, on the other hand — they're all about ONE statement piece, lots of breathing room, and a palette that's barely-there.

So — what ARE the main design principles for wall displays? Balance, scale, contrast, harmony, alignment, and spacing… those SIX are your foundation.

Together they turn a random collection of prints into something that feels CURATED — like chapters in a really good book, you know?

How do you balance contrast and harmony? Let one piece lead — bolder frame, stronger tone — then let the others ECHO it quietly rather than compete.

And for a cohesive gallery wall? Plan on the floor, pick a shared colour story, keep spacing CONSISTENT… those three alone make a massive difference.

Elements of art versus principles of design — quickly: ELEMENTS are the raw materials (line, colour, shape, texture) and principles are the RULES for how you use them.

[gently] The seven core principles — balance, contrast, harmony, scale, alignment, spacing, and emphasis — think of them as a checklist every time you hang something new.

Once you start seeing these principles everywhere… honestly, your whole approach to choosing and placing art just CHANGES.

A little tip I love: start with a SET of prints that ALREADY share a colour story — it does half the harmony work for you before you even hang them.

[warmly] And if you want that Japandi-inspired, utterly calm wall… something like this is exactly where I'd start — three prints, one shared mood, done.

[sighs] Honestly… these principles have been around for centuries because they WORK — and once you know them, every wall you style just feels more like YOU.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
